subject: Rollforward regression — p99 spike impacting ZenithHealth production
messages:
From: Samir Desai <samir@zenithhealth.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia.park@zenithhealth.com>, ZenithHealth SRE <sre@zenithhealth.com>
Date: 2028-10-04T09:12:00Z
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 latency increase after latest model rollout

Aditya —

We started seeing significant tail latency in our Redwood-hosted API integration at ~08:45 PDT after the model rollout you performed (variant v2.7.1). Our dashboards show p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s and p99 to ~3.8s on production traffic. The errors are mostly timeouts (503) from the API gateway and higher queueing. This is impacting our clinical-scheduling flow (request IDs in attached p99_spike_sample_ids.txt). Can you confirm whether a rollout went through and advise next steps?

We're pausing dependency on non-critical flows but urgent for the scheduling path. Attaching a Grafana snapshot and a short tail log.

Thanks,
Samir Desai
Head of Platform Engineering
ZenithHealth

Attachments: p99_spike_sample_ids.txt, grafana-spike-screenshot.png, ZenithHealth-prod-requests.log

From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Desai <samir@zenithhealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-04T09:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency increase after latest model rollout

Samir — thanks for the quick flag. I can confirm a targeted rollout (route: zenithhealth-prod -> model v2.7.1) completed at 08:30 PDT with a 10% canary split. We're immediately pausing further rollout and I have engineering on it.

Quick ask: can you confirm the top request IDs from the attachment that still show p99s? Also, if you can share the sample payload shape (PII redacted) it helps reproduce. We'll triage KV cache behavior, batch sizing, and kernel selection mismatches as suspects.

I'll loop in Rishi (serving/runtime) and Lauren for higher-level coordination. My current plan: 1) halt and pin rollouts for Zenith, 2) snapshot canary traffic, 3) if impact persists, roll back the canary variant. ETA for first update: 30–45m.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Account Lead, Strategic Customer Success
Redwood Inference

---

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-04T09:52:00Z
Subject: RE: Sudden p95/p99 latency increase after latest model rollout

Aditya / Ben —

I dug into the canary traces. Initial observations:
- Model v2.7.1 changes attention layout and increases KV-cache footprint for long-context prompts; this causes higher cache miss rates on hosts configured with the conservative KV cache size.
- Autoscaler metrics show an uptick in queue length and request serialization time, correlating with the deployment window.
- There was also a change in the dynamic batcher heuristics in the last runtime push that increases max-batch-wait for low QPS routes. Combined, it's amplifying the tail for long requests.

Immediate mitigations I recommend:
1) Pin Zenith route to v2.7.0 (previous variant) — this is the fastest rollback and low risk.
2) Temporarily reduce max-batch-wait to 8ms for the route to avoid oversized batching on latency-sensitive flows.
3) Increase KV cache allocation on the canary pool (if rollback is not possible immediately).

I'll prepare a one-click rollback and a playbook — need a thumbs-up from Aditya to proceed. I can implement (1) in ~15m and (2) in ~10m thereafter.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@zenithhealth.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Desai <samir@zenithhealth.com>, ZenithHealth SRE <sre@zenithhealth.com>
Date: 2028-10-04T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency increase after latest model rollout

Aditya / Rishi —

Thanks for the quick triage. We are seeing the same request patterns in the IDs attached; most of the problematic calls are the longer scheduling prompts (context ~1.8–2k tokens). A rollback to v2.7.0 would be ideal. Please let us know when the rollback completes so we can re-enable the dependent flow.

Olivia
Senior SW Eng — Integrations
ZenithHealth

From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-04T10:20:00Z
Subject: Exec sync + credit offer for ZenithHealth outage / p99 spike

Lauren / Ben / Marissa —

Heads-up: ZenithHealth (strategic) is experiencing a production-impacting p99 spike after the v2.7.1 canary. Customer requests rollback to v2.7.0. Rishi has a rollback ready; he can execute in ~15m.

Customer impact: scheduling flow degraded (partial pause by customer). Potential executive attention if not resolved within the hour. Recommendation: approve a goodwill service credit (one week of usage for impacted route) and prepare an incident brief for the CTO. Can you confirm approval to proceed with the credit and who will handle the executive outreach?

I'll execute the rollback pending approval. Notifying legal not required yet but keeping sales/AM looped.

—Aditya
Account Lead

Date: 2028-10-05T18:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Rollforward regression — p99 spike impacting ZenithHealth production — resolution and next steps

Samir / Olivia —

Thanks again for your patience. Quick update and resolution timeline: 
- 2028-10-04 10:35 PDT: Redwood executed a rollback of Zenith route to model v2.7.0 and reduced max-batch-wait to 8ms for the route.
- 2028-10-04 10:50 PDT: Observed p95/p99 metrics return to baseline (p95 ~110–140ms, p99 ~270–320ms).
- Impact: customer scheduling flow restored; no further 503s observed for the tested sample IDs.

Next actions:
1) Incident postmortem (owner: Rishi) with root cause analysis on KV cache sizing & batcher heuristic interaction — due 2028-10-09.
2) Engineering action items: add a canary gate for KV-cache-sensitive variants, add regression e2e test for long-context latency, and refine rollout policy for low-latency routes.
3) Customer follow-up: Ben will send an executive note and Marissa will coordinate the goodwill credit (one week of usage for impacted route) and schedule a joint postmortem review session.

Attached: grafana-spike-screenshot.png, incident-playbook-snippet.pdf (snippet).

Apologies for the disruption — we'll share the full postmortem and action plan by the target date.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: grafana-spike-screenshot.png, incident-playbook-snippet.pdf
